video_goal: Demonstrate the precise folding sequence to create a Suzanne dart-style paper airplane.
single_prompt: A top-down view shows bare human hands placing a crisp white standard A4 sheet of paper flat on a natural wood grain table under bright, even overhead studio lighting. The camera shifts to an over-the-shoulder view as the hands fold the paper in half lengthwise, pressing firmly along the left edge. A close-up reveals the hands unfolding the paper flat to show the center crease. From a top-down view, the right hand folds the top-right corner down to the center crease, followed by the left hand folding the top-left corner to form a sharp triangular peak. In a close-up, the hands fold the newly formed right diagonal edge inward flush against the center crease, then repeat on the left side to create a narrow dart shape. A side angle captures the index finger and thumb folding the sharp top point down about one inch for a blunt nose. From an over-the-shoulder view, the hands fold the entire paper in half along the original center crease. A close-up shows the right hand folding the top flap down to create the first wing, leaving a half-inch fuselage gap. The camera moves to a top-down view as the hands flip the plane over and fold the second wing down to align perfectly with the first. In a close-up, thumbs pinch the outer trailing edges of both wings, folding them up slightly to form half-inch vertical winglets. Finally, from a first-person view, the hands open the wings outward to a slight upward 'V' angle, holding the finished Suzanne dart-style plane toward the camera over the flat natural wood grain table under bright, even overhead studio lighting.
